findings.title: MCP connect cannot create message flows
findings.why_it_matters: The collaboration feature is exposed through the MCP connect tool, but the handler always calls the engine without a connection type. A cross-participant request therefore defaults to SequenceFlow and is rejected, so callers cannot create the required collaboration-level MessageFlow even though the engine supports it.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a connection type (with a MessageFlow option) to the connect tool schema, destructure it in the handler, and pass it to SimpleBpmnEngine.connect; add a handler-level two-pool message-flow test.
evidence: src/server/handlers.ts:368 destructures only sourceId, targetId, label, and condition; line 371 calls engine.connect with no type, so the engine default is bpmn:SequenceFlow.
src/server/tools.ts:232-255 exposes no type property, while SimpleBpmnEngine.connect accepts bpmn:MessageFlow and the focused engine test creates one only by calling the engine directly.

A two-pool MCP sequence using connect({sourceId:'Task_1', targetId:'Task_2', type:'bpmn:MessageFlow'}) returns 'Sequence flows cannot cross process or nested-scope boundaries' because the extra property is ignored.

findings.title: Mermaid pools share one process and sequence flows
findings.why_it_matters: Mermaid subgraphs are emitted as multiple participants that all reference the single generated process, while every node and edge is owned by that same process. A conversion with two pools therefore loses per-pool process ownership and emits cross-pool edges as sequence flows instead of collaboration MessageFlows, violating the collaboration semantic contract.
findings.suggested_fix: Create or select a process root for each subgraph, assign subgraph nodes to that owner, and classify edges whose endpoints have different owners as collaboration MessageFlows; keep same-owner edges as SequenceFlows in their owning process.
evidence: src/core/SimpleBpmnGenerator.ts:29 creates one process document; lines 54-70 assign every generated node ownerId/scopeId to that processId.
src/core/SimpleBpmnGenerator.ts:92-103 assigns every edge bpmn:SequenceFlow with ownerId/scopeId processId before subgraphs are converted.

src/core/SimpleBpmnGenerator.ts:107-123 creates each participant with processRef: processId. Generating an AST with two subgraphs produces Process_1.flowElements containing both tasks and Flow_2, and both participants processRef Process_1.

residual_risks: Participant structural properties are not synchronized on updateElement: changing properties.blackBox or properties.processRef does not update the participant processRef field or process-root lifecycle.
The serializer validates ownership at mutation time, but imported XML with cross-scope connection references is not independently rejected before it is reserialized.
testing_gaps: No MCP handler/tool test exercises creating a MessageFlow between nodes owned by different participant processes.
No Mermaid conversion test asserts that subgraph participants have distinct process refs and that cross-subgraph edges become collaboration MessageFlows.
